title: Reinforcement of the Aft Cargo Compartment Sill Frames at Stations C58 to C64

issue.reason: Original issue of the aft cargo sill frame reinforcement proposal dossier.

abstract: Local reinforcement of the aft cargo compartment sill between stations C58 and C64 by a machined titanium load-diffusion strap, answering repeated cycle-driven cracking at the frame lower flange on high-utilisation CIRRANE-13 aircraft.

sections.reason: Since early 2024 five operators have reported cracking at the lower flange of the aft cargo compartment sill frames on CIRRANE-13 aircraft in short-sector operation. Seventeen findings have been recorded across a population of roughly 150 aircraft, the earliest at 20 400 flight cycles, and all but two of them on the left-hand side where the compartment sill carries the loading rail reaction. Four findings were outside the allowable damage limits of the applicable repair scheme and needed an engineering repair with a life limit attached. The type reaches its cycle milestones far faster than its flight-hour milestones, so the population at risk grows quickly, and the corrosion-resistant doubler standard already embodied on these aircraft did not change the cracking rate, which points at the load path rather than at the environment.
sections.description: A machined titanium load-diffusion strap is installed on the inboard face of the sill frames between stations C58 and C64, spanning the lower flange run-out where the loading rail reaction is introduced. The strap spreads the reaction across three frame bays and reduces the peak stress at the flange radius by an estimated 27 per cent. The frame rib D5331113688429 is retained and locally re-drilled, the lower intercostal D5331115152546 is replaced by a thicker item, and a new stiffener PEL822344-24 is added at the flange run-out. The joint is fastened with tension head bolts AGS713311K3 into the existing skin doubler D5331121169495, which is the reason the aircraft has to be at the corrosion-resistant doubler standard before this modification can be embodied. Revised detail is on drawings D53311163012 and D53311194420. Access is through the aft cargo compartment, zones 131, 132, 135 and 141, with the lining and floor panels removed between the two stations. The strap footprint runs within 20 mm of the aft fuselage wiring terminal block 3482VC and the clearance to it is one of the items to be confirmed.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 7.8 kg per aircraft, offset to the left of the centre line, with a lateral moment below the reporting threshold and a longitudinal centre-of-gravity shift under 0.04 per cent MAC. No electrical load change. The modification is not interchangeable with the pre-modification standard because the frame drilling pattern changes and the strap cannot be removed without replacing the intercostal. The repeat detailed visual inspection of the sill region can be withdrawn once a revised fatigue substantiation is accepted. Maintenance manual, illustrated parts and repair content for the aft fuselage all need updating, and at least one existing repair scheme will have to be re-issued because the strap occupies the area it uses.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only at this stage. The provisional estimate is five days inside a scheduled C-check on the assumption that the aft cargo compartment is already open for other work. A production cut-in is not proposed until the retrofit design is frozen and the loading rail reaction is re-measured on a delivered aircraft.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must confirm the clearance between the strap footprint and the aft fuselage wiring run, whether the existing aft lower shell repair scheme survives embodiment, whether the cargo lining panel standard fitted to later aircraft still fits over the strap, and whether the retrofit Service Bulletin for the corrosion-resistant doubler needs an ordering constraint added to its effectivity statement.

type_data.balance_impact: Left-hand installation, lateral moment below reporting threshold, longitudinal CG shift under 0.04 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in proposed at this stage
